plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flat, pointed stems and tubular, asymmetrical flowers that dangle from the stem tips. Widely grown as a houseplant in the Northern Hemisphere, where it blooms in response to short days and cool nights.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: In the wild it grows on tree branches and rocks in humid forests, and it needs about 12-14 hours of darkness each night for several weeks to set buds.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy 'flowers' are actually colored bracts surrounding tiny yellow true flowers called cyathia. In frost-free climates it grows into a large shrub several meters tall, while in colder regions it is a popular potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in warm regions such as California, Florida, Australia, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used its sap for medicine and its bracts to make reddish dye. Its color change is triggered by long nights, just like the Thanksgiving cactus.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with cylindrical flower spikes made of numerous bright red stamens that resemble a bottle brush. Its blooms are rich in nectar and attract honeyeaters, lorikeets, and bees during the Southern Hemisphere late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to January), with sporadic blooms at other times
plants.location: Native to eastern Australia; widely planted in warm regions including California, the Mediterranean, and South Africa
plants.funFact: The woody seed capsules can remain on the stems for years and often release seeds only after fire or branch death.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pink. It flowers in cold weather, often pushing through snow in mild winter gardens and woodlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe, from the Alps to the northern Apennines and the Balkans; cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.
